subject: POC Trial: Environment & Success Criteria (Acme Health)
messages:

Subject: POC Trial: Environment & Success Criteria (Acme Health)

Hi Eric - thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned for the trial kickoff:

Summary of the ask:
- Evaluate Redwood Inference for clinical document summarization and structured extraction across a 3-week trial.
- Success criteria: 95%+ accuracy on the gold prompt set for summarization (measured by your QA team), sustained 200 RPS peak with median latencies <200ms for single-turn generation, and end-to-end cost estimate within the projected budget.

POC evaluation plan (proposed):
1) Week 0 (Prep, 3 business days): environment provisioning, sample data ingest, network/security checklist.
2) Week 1 (Baseline runs): run initial prompts on hosted API and dedicated sandbox variants - collect perf/cost/quality.
3) Week 2 (Optimization): iterate on batching, caching, and quantization profiles; run final eval prompts.
4) Week 3 (Wrap & Handoff): review results, produce scorecard, and next-steps for production.

Environment options (we discussed tradeoffs on the call):
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood-hosted API - easiest to start, limited VPC access. Good for a quick baseline.
- Dedicated sandbox: reserved GPU pool for Acme - predictable throughput, isolated data, ideal if you need consistent latency and full debugging access.
- VPC trial (Private): private deployment in your VPC - required for strict data governance and if your security team needs no egress. Longer lead time for networking and approvals.

What we need from Acme to choose and provision the environment:
- Security preference: Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC (if VPC, we’ll need an initial network contact + firewall rules).
- Expected dataset size for trial (GB) and sample rate for real-time ingestion.
- Estimated concurrency and peak RPS.
- SOC 2 / KMS requirements (if encryption keys must be customer-managed).

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm environment preference and provide a networking contact (if applicable) by EOD Wed 24-Mar.
- I’ve attached a one-page POC scope and a network checklist for your security team to review.
- Once environment is selected we’ll schedule a 60-min kickoff (SE + CS + you + network/infra).

Attachments: poc-scope.docx, network-checklist.xlsx

Thanks - happy to adjust timelines based on your availability.

--

Subject: Re: POC Trial: Environment & Success Criteria (Acme Health)

Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. We’re excited to move forward. A few items from our side:

1) Security preference: We’d prefer a Dedicated sandbox for the POC. Our security and privacy teams are open to Hosted for an initial proof-of-concept, but given patient data (de-identified) and our internal policy, Dedicated is the safer ask.
2) Dataset size: ~40 GB of de-identified clinical notes for the trial; we can provide a 5% live stream sample for real-time ingestion tests.
3) Concurrency/RPS: Target peak 200 RPS, sustained 50-80 RPS during typical hours.
4) SOC 2/KMS: We need SOC 2 Type II evidence and will require customer-managed KMS for any production move; for the trial we can accept Redwood-managed keys if Dedicated is isolated.

Network contact: I’m looping Ashley (procurement) and Brad Kim (security) - Ashley will coordinate procurement timelines. Brad (cc’d) will follow-up on firewall rules and any evidence requests.

Please go ahead and put Aditya on the thread for SE planning and Evelyn for onboarding. We can target a kickoff next Tue 24-Mar if that works for your team.

Thanks -
Eric
Director, AI Initiatives
Acme Health

Subject: Re: POC Trial: Environment & Success Criteria (Acme Health)

Thanks Eric - good context. A few technical notes and recommendations for the Dedicated sandbox setup so we can hit your targets:

- Instance sizing: for 200 RPS peak we recommend a pool of 4 x A100-80GB equivalent for steady-state throughput, with autoscaling to 6 nodes for peak bursts. If you expect long sequences (4k+ tokens per request) we should size memory accordingly.
- Batching: we’ll enable adaptive batching with a 25ms max latency headroom to reduce cost during steady load.
- KV/cache: we’ll enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (helps with clinical templates).
- Data ingest: please provide a sample S3 location and IAM role; for initial runs we can accept a temporary pre-signed bucket.

Attachments: se-config-recs.pdf (detailed config + network port list).

Next steps from SE: once procurement confirms Dedicated sandbox, I’ll provision a test pool, run a smoke test against your sample data, and share a perf/cost baseline report within 2 business days.
